id: 第四章-终点篇-河童-十二-p1

en: 第四章-终点篇-河童-十二
One afternoon, it was a little cold.
u.src: 一个下午，稍微有点冷。

en: I grew tired of reading Words of a Fool, so I went to visit the philosopher Maro.
u.src: 我读《傻子的话》读到厌烦，就去拜访哲学家马咯。

en: As I was walking through town, I saw a kappa as thin as a mosquito leaning against a wall in a quiet corner, staring blankly.
u.src: 我走在街上，在一个僻静的角落，看见一只瘦得像蚊子一样的河童靠着墙发呆呢。

en: Wasn't this the very kappa who had stolen my fountain pen before?
u.src: 这不就是以前偷过我的钢笔的那只河童嘛。

en: Thinking, Now I've got you, I quickly called out to a powerful-looking kappa policeman who happened to be passing by.
u.src: 我心想：这下可逮到你了，急忙叫住刚好从那里经过的一个身材威猛的河童警察。

en: Please help me catch that kappa.
u.src: “请您帮忙抓住那只河童。

en: About a month ago, he stole my fountain pen.
u.src: 一个来月之前，他偷了我的钢笔。”

en: The policeman raised the club he was holding in his right hand (in that country policemen do not carry swords, but usually use clubs made of mizumatsu wood) and shouted at the kappa, "Hey!"
u.src: 警察举起右手拿着的棍子（这个国家的警察不佩剑，常用的是水松木制棍子），对着那只河童喊了声：“喂！”

en: I thought the kappa might run away.
u.src: 我想那只河童可能会逃跑。

en: To my surprise, he calmly walked up to the policeman, folded his arms, and looked arrogantly at both my face and the policeman's.
u.src: 意外的是他却沉着地走到警察跟前，双臂交叉，傲慢地看着着我和警察的脸。

en: The policeman did not get angry either; he took a notebook from the pouch on his belly and began questioning him: “What is your name?”
u.src: 警察也并不愤怒，就从肚袋里取出记事簿，开始审问他：“叫什么名字？”
“咯噜喀。”

en: What do you do for a living?
u.src: “做职业呢？”

en: He was still a mail carrier just two or three days ago.
u.src: “两三天以前还是个邮递员。”

en: All right. This man says you stole his fountain pen. Is that true?
u.src: “好的。这个人说你偷了他的钢笔，确有此事吗？”

en: Yes, I stole it about a month ago.
u.src: “是的，一个来月以前偷的。”

en: What are you stealing it for?
u.src: “偷去做什么呢？”

en: I want to give it to a child as a toy.
u.src: “想拿给小孩当玩具。”
“小孩呢？”

en: Only then did the policeman look sharply at that kappa.
u.src: 警察这才目光炯炯地看了那只河童一眼。
“一个星期以前，死掉了。”

en: Do you have your death certificate with you?
u.src: “带着死亡证明书吗？”

en: The kappa, thin as a mosquito, took a sheet of paper from his belly pouch.
u.src: 瘦成蚊子一样的河童从肚袋里取出一张纸。

en: The policeman glanced at it, then suddenly smiled, patted him on the shoulder, and said, "All right, good work."
u.src: 警察看了一下，忽然微笑地拍了拍他的肩膀说：“好的，辛苦啦。”

en: I stared blankly at the policeman.
u.src: 我呆呆地看着警察。

en: At that moment, the thin kappa muttered to himself and left us behind.
u.src: 这个时候，瘦河童喃喃自语地扔下我们走掉了。

en: I came to my senses and asked the policeman, "Why don't you catch that kappa?"
u.src: 我回过神来，问警察：“你为什么不抓那只河童？”
“他没有罪。”

en: But he stole my fountain pen...
u.src: “但是他偷了我的钢笔……”

ja: するためではなかったのですか
en: Was he not meant to be a toy for the child?
u.src: “他不是为了给孩子当玩具吗？

en: But that child is already dead now.
u.src: 但是那孩子如今已经死了。

en: If you have any doubts, please consult Article 1285 of the Criminal Code.
u.src: 你要是有什么疑问，请查阅刑法第一千二百八十五条。”

en: As soon as I finished speaking, the policeman left me behind and went away.
u.src: 话刚说完，警察也撇下我走了。

en: I had no choice but to keep repeating “Article 1285 of the Criminal Code” as I hurried to Malo’s house.
u.src: 我不得不反复念叨“刑法第一千二百八十五条”，赶紧到马咯家去。

en: Malo the philosopher was a very hospitable kappa.
u.src: 哲学家马咯是个非常好客的河童。

en: In the dim room were Judge Pep, Doctor Chack, and even Gal, the manager of the glass company; beneath the seven-colored glass lantern, smoke hung thick in the air.
u.src: 幽暗的房间里，审判官培卟、医生查喀，玻璃公司经理嘎尔都在此呢，七彩玻璃灯笼下，烟雾缭绕。

en: It was extremely convenient for me that Judge Pep was there.
u.src: 审判官培卟在场，对我来说十分正好。

en: I sat in the chair and, without even stopping to look up Article 1285 of the penal code,
u.src: 我坐在椅子上，顾不上去查刑法第一千二百八十五条，

ja: しかしすぐにペップに
en: I immediately asked Pepp, "Pepp, forgive me for speaking plainly,
u.src: 却立刻问培卟：“培卟君，恕我直言，

en: does this country really not punish criminals?"
u.src: 这个国家难道不处分罪犯吗？”

en: Pepp, holding a premium cigarette between his lips, elegantly blew a smoke ring, then said casually, "Of course there must be punishment; even the death penalty is possible."
u.src: 叼着高级香烟的培卟，优雅的吐了一口烟圈，然后漫不经心地说，“自然要处分，死刑也有呢。”
“但是我一个来月以前……”

en: I explained the whole matter from beginning to end, then asked him what Article 1285 of the Penal Code meant.
u.src: 我把事情的前前后后说了一遍，接着询问他刑法第一千二百八十五条是如何的。

ja: 「うん、こういうことです。『どんな
en: Well, it is like this: 'No matter what crime he committed, once the motive that led him to commit it has disappeared, the offender can no longer be punished.'
u.src: “嗯，是这样的：‘无论犯了什么罪行，导致他犯罪的动机一旦消失，那么就不能处分犯罪者了。’

en: As for your case, that kappa once had a son, but now his son is dead, so the crime he committed has been wiped out.
u.src: 就你这事而言，那只河童以前有过儿子，但是现在他儿子已经死了，所以他所犯的罪也就一笔勾销了。”
“这非常不合理啦。”
“别搞笑啦。

en: It would be unreasonable to treat the kappa who is no longer a father the same as the kappa who still is one.
u.src: 对不再是父亲的河童和仍然是父亲的河童同等对待，那才是不合理呢。

en: Yes, yes, under Japanese law, they have to be treated equally.
u.src: 对，对，按照日本的法律，是要一视同仁的。

en: From our point of view, it seems rather funny.
u.src: 在我们看来，觉得挺搞笑的。
呵呵。”

en: Peppu tossed away his cigarette butt and gave a listless little laugh.
u.src: 培卟扔掉烟蒂，无精打采的笑了笑。

en: At that moment, Chuck, who did not know much about the law, cut in.
u.src: 这个时候后，对法律了解不多的查喀插话进来。

en: He adjusted his pince-nez and asked me, "Does Japan have the death penalty too?"
u.src: 他扶了扶夹鼻眼镜，问我：“日本也有死刑吗？”

ja: うまでもありませんよ！
u.src: “这还用说哦！

en: In Japan it is hanging, you know.
u.src: 日本是绞刑呢。”

en: Pepp's indifference annoyed me, so I took the chance to make a sarcastic remark,
u.src: 冷漠的培卟让我心里不快，就乘机嘲讽了一句，

en: The death penalty in your country must be even more civilized than Japan's, I suppose?
u.src: “贵国的死刑比日本更加文明呢吧？”

en: “Naturally, it is more civilized,” Pepp remained calm,
u.src: “自然要更文明喽，”培卟依旧保持冷静，

en: “In our country we do not use hanging.
u.src: “我们国家不用绞刑。

en: Sometimes we use the electric chair once, but most of the time even that is unnecessary,
u.src: 间或用一次电刑，但在大部分时候，连电刑也用不上，

en: we merely announce the charge and inform the criminal.”
u.src: 只是宣告罪名通知犯人而已。”

en: Will the kappa die just like that?
u.src: “就这样，河童就会去死吗？”
“当然。

en: A kappa's nervous system is far more sensitive than a human's.
u.src: 河童的神经系统要比人类的敏锐的多呢。”

en: It is not only used for executions.
u.src: “不光是死刑。

en: It is also used as a means of murder...
u.src: 也被作为谋杀的手段……”

en: Master Gael said with a kindly smile, his whole face lit by the purple glow of the stained glass,
u.src: 嘎尔老板满脸映照着彩色玻璃的紫光，亲切的笑着说，

en: The other day, a socialist slandered me by calling me a thief,
u.src: “前一阵，有个社会主义者污蔑我‘是小偷’，

en: and I nearly had a heart attack.
u.src: 我险些犯了心脏病。”

en: There are unexpectedly many cases like this.
u.src: “这种情况多的出人意料呢。

en: A lawyer I knew was killed by exactly this kind of method.
u.src: 我认识的一个律师就是被这种手段害死的。”

en: The philosopher Magg cut in and said.
u.src: 哲学家马咯插嘴说。

en: I turned my head and looked at him.
u.src: 我扭头看了看他。

en: His eyes were not looking at anyone, and he said with his usual mocking smile:
u.src: 他目光没看任何人，像平时一样讥讽的笑着说：

en: I do not know who it was, but someone slandered that kappa by calling him a frog—
u.src: “不知道是谁，污蔑那只河童是青蛙——

en: You must know this, I suppose,
u.src: 你应该知道这个吧，

en: In this country, being called a frog is the same as being cursed as a beast.
u.src: 在这个国家，被称作青蛙就等于被骂作畜生。

en: —All day long he kept wondering: am I a frog?
u.src: ——他整天怀疑：我是青蛙吗？

en: Surely I am not a frog, am I?
u.src: 不是青蛙吧？

en: And so he died in depression.
u.src: 抑郁而终了。”

en: This is probably suicide, isn't it?
u.src: “这应该是自杀吧。”

en: That kappa who said the lawyer was a frog said it in order to kill the lawyer.
u.src: “说律师是青蛙那个河童，就是为了杀死律师才说的。

ja: ということになるでしょう……」
en: From your point of view, I suppose that counts as suicide too...
u.src: 从你们的角度来看，这也算自杀喽……”

en: Before Magg had finished speaking, a sharp pistol shot suddenly rang out from the house of Tock, the poet next door, shaking the sky.
u.src: 马咯话音没落，突然从隔壁诗人托喀家——传来了尖锐的手枪声，震彻天空。
